LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: STORY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story, part of Strand 4 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we make stories interesting in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. highlight features of an interesting story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write an interesting story based on the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy writing imaginative stories.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. highlight features of an interesting story,

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write an interesting story based on the theme,

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy writing imaginative stories.

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to highlight features of an interesting story,

2. team up to collect and put together interesting stories from their community,

3. collaboratively hold storytelling sessions on the theme,

4. create a collection of vocabulary from the stories they have read,

5. search for interesting pictures relevant to the theme from print and non-print sources,

6. write an interesting story based on the pictures retrieved,

7. present the written stories in class for peer review,

8. organise their stories in a class portfolio,

9. publish their written stories in a school or children’s magazine.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to highlight features of an interesting story,
2. team up to collect and put together interesting stories from their community,
3. collaboratively hold storytelling sessions on the theme,
4. create a collection of vocabulary from the stories they have read,
5. search for interesting pictures relevant to the theme from print and non-print sources,
6. write an interesting story based on the pictures retrieved,
7. present the written stories in class for peer review,
8. organise their stories in a class portfolio,
9. publish their written stories in a school or children’s magazine.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing: Story together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner engages with new ideas that ignite creative thinking when writing

an interesting story based on the pictures retrieved.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows defining personal skills when narrating stories before peers during the

storytelling sessions.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is achieved as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when searching for interesting pictures from

print and non-print sources.

• Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays transparency when giving honest opinions about peers’ work during

review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Healthy interpersonal relationships: This is enhanced as the learner harmoniously relates with peers during storytelling sessions

and peer reviews.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of conflict resolution to their learning of similar concepts in Social Studies and Religious

Education.
